findings.reason: the repair wave should route every receipt through the existing writer/stamp so the contract is one implementation, not sixteen near-copies.
findings.text: the render-only entry point defines its own `_write_json` (+ `certificate._strict` + `allow_nan` variant) that is copied into its sibling drivers (`benchmarks/limited_row_shadow_census.py:125`, `benchmarks/xpoint_cell_wedge_oracle.py:197`, `benchmarks/exact_clip_seed_amplitude.py:80`, `benchmarks/coupling_moment_order_evaluation.py`), while the owner `benchmarks/solovev_certificate._write_json` at `benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py:250` already performs the same strict JSON write, and none of the six sampled render-only drivers calls the owner's `stamp_source_revision` (`benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py:280`), so the receipt-revision contract forks per driver too

findings.reason: the measured 1002-file extent means the fix belongs in the path owner once, not as a per-directory rewrite of the regenerated receipts.
findings.text: render receipts record path fields by ad-hoc string handling rather than through the `FilePath` owner, and 1002 committed files under `docs/figures/` carry absolute `.reckon-worktrees` paths that dangle once the worktree is reclaimed (e.g. `docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/exact-clip-low-state/receipt.json`), while the plan's open followup `f-fsa-render-receipt-relative-paths` scopes the repair only to the regenerated directories

findings.reason: one stamp owner already exists and is already the repair target elsewhere; extending it to render receipts removes a second revision contract rather than adding one.
findings.text: the plan's §3 render-receipt mechanism duplicates the existing source-revision stamp instead of extending it: the owner exposes `_source_revision`/`stamp_source_revision` and the production-route writers were repaired (followup `f-fsa-production-route-receipt-revision`) to route through it, yet the render-only receipt writers emit their own revision handling and no render receipt sampled carries the owner's stamp

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan's one genuinely new module, `tests/renderer_wall_scan.py` (a scanner exposing a small `scan()` over AST traversal), hides substantial walk-and-classify behaviour behind a narrow interface, and the tree-wide guard `tests/test_renderer_contours_inside_wall.py` consumes that one scanner rather than re-walking the tree.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — render receipts re-implement path resolution per driver instead of using the `FilePath` owner, and the defect the plan already tracks as open is measured here at 1002 files, far wider than the followup's scope.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan extends the existing owners rather than forking them: `nova/media/poloidal.py` painters (`draw_scattered_contours`, `draw_flux_contours(wall=)`), the `benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py` certificate/stamp machinery, and the standard reckon evidence/ledger conventions; no painter, receipt store or scanner owner is the entry point it duplicates.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan's render-only repair wave adds a per-driver receipt builder (`_write_json` plus a schema string) over behaviour the certificate owner already supplies, and the plan never says why the owner cannot be extended.
